bib.title: OpenHands: An Open Platform for AI Software Developers as Generalist Agents

question: How can an open platform give AI agents a shared architecture, sandboxed runtime, tool library, multi-agent delegation and evaluation harness for software-developer-style work?
hypothesis: A single generalist agent built on a general code-based action space (CodeAct) can be competitive across software, web and assistance tasks without task-specific prompts.
contributions: Event stream interaction mechanism between UI, agents and environments (Sec 2.1)
Docker-sandboxed runtime with bash, IPython and Playwright browser (Sec 2.2)
AgentSkills library as extensible agent-computer interface (Sec 2.3)

method.summary: A community MIT-licensed platform: agents map event history to an action, a Docker runtime maps actions to observations, both recorded in an event stream. Authors evaluate its CodeActAgent, BrowsingAgent and GPTSwarm agents on 15 benchmarks with off-the-shelf LLMs and compare to published baselines.
method.task: agent platform; software engineering, web browsing, misc assistance benchmarks

inference.samples: inferred: one run per model and benchmark; no repeats, seeds or CIs reported
inference.prompting: CodeActAgent default system prompt unchanged across categories; BrowsingAgent zero-shot (Appendix K); CodeActSWEAgent uses an in-context demonstration from SWE-agent (App H)

parameters.MINT iterations: up to five, two solution proposals

metrics.name: Success Rate

metrics.name: $ Avg. Cost

eval.protocol: Single reported number per cell; baseline numbers taken from published papers with different models; no variance.

prompts.text:
# Instructions
Review the current state of the page and all other information to find the best possible next action to accomplish your goal. Your answer will be interpreted and executed by a program, make sure to follow the formatting instructions.
prompts.where: Appendix K, p35 (full prompt with action space continues to p38; WebArena adds concise-answer example)

results.claim: CodeActAgent v1.8 with claude-3-5-sonnet resolves 26.0% of SWE-Bench Lite, competitive with open-source SWE specialists but not leading.
results.setup: SWE-Bench Lite, 300 instances, no hint text, CodeActAgent v1.8, claude-3-5-sonnet@20240620; baselines use other models and were not re-run as far as stated
results.table: Table 4, row OH CodeActAgent v1.8 claude-3-5-sonnet@20240620, column Success Rate (%)

results.claim: With gpt-4o, CodeActAgent v1.8 resolves 22.0% of SWE-Bench Lite; with gpt-4o-mini 7.0%.
results.note: gpt-4o-mini is 6.3 in Table 3 but 7.0 in Table 4.
results.table: Table 4, row OH CodeActAgent v1.8 gpt-4o-2024-05-13, column Success Rate (%)

results.claim: Average cost per SWE-Bench Lite instance for CodeActAgent v1.8 with claude-3-5-sonnet was $1.10.
results.setup: SWE-Bench Lite, CodeActAgent v1.8, claude-3-5-sonnet; column is '$ Avg. Cost', per-unit not stated (footnote 2 implies per instance)
results.table: Table 4, row OH CodeActAgent v1.8 claude-3-5-sonnet@20240620, column $ Avg. Cost

results.claim: The authors argue the same CodeAct agent, with no change to its system prompt, is competitive across software, web and misc tasks; this is the generality claim.
results.setup: authors' reading of Table 3; web via delegation to BrowsingAgent, GAIA figure comes from GPTSwarm not CodeAct
results.quote: the same CodeAct agent, without any modifications to its system prompt, demonstrates competitive performance across three major task categories

results.claim: Full SWE-Bench (2294 instances) is estimated to cost $6.9k.
results.quote: Running the complete set of 2294 instances costs $6.9k, using a conservative estimate of $3 per instance.

results.claim: A SWE-Bench Lite evaluation with gpt-4o costs around 600 USD.
results.quote: Running a SWE-Bench Lite Jimenez et al. (2024) evaluation with gpt-4o costs around 600 USD.

results.claim: Integration tests mock all LLM calls with predefined responses matched on exact prompts and compare outputs against gold files; no effectiveness figure is given.
results.setup: run on every PR and main commit on Linux and Mac, local/SSH/exec sandboxes
results.quote: the framework intercepts all LLM calls and supplies predefined responses based on exact prompt matches

results.claim: A skill is added to AgentSkills only if the LLM cannot easily write the code itself or it calls an external model.
results.quote: We only add a new skill when: (1) it is not readily achievable for LLM to write code directly

results.claim: Each task session spins up an isolated Docker container reached via a REST API server inside it; isolation is asserted, not tested.
results.quote: For each task session, OpenHands spins up a securely isolated docker container sandbox, where all the actions from the event stream are executed.

results.claim: HumanEvalFix Python: CodeActAgent v1.5 gpt-4o fixes 79.3%, below SWE-agent 1-shot 87.7%.
results.setup: 164 instances, Python split, 0-shot, pass@k following Muennighoff et al. 2024; SWE-agent was given a 1-shot demonstration
results.note: Paper says 'almost doubling' StarCoder2-15B (48.6); 79.3/48.6 is about 1.63x.
results.quote: OpenHands CodeActAgent successfully fixes 79.3% of bugs in the Python split.

results.claim: ML-Bench: CodeActAgent v1.5 gpt-4o 76.5%, above Aider 64.4 and SWE-Agent 42.6.
results.table: Table 4, ML-Bench, row OH CodeActAgent v1.5 gpt-2024-05-13 gpt-4o, column Success Rate (%)

results.claim: BIRD: CodeActAgent v1.5 gpt-4o 47.3% execution accuracy.

results.table: Table 4, BIRD, row OH CodeActAgent v1.5 gpt-4o-2024-05-13, column Success Rate (%)

results.setup: 136 instances, up to five iterations, two chances to propose solutions
results.table: Table 6, MINT code subset, row OH CodeActAgent v1.5 gpt-4o-2024-05-13, column Success Rate (%)

results.claim: GPQA across subsets: CodeActAgent v1.5 gpt-4o scores 53.1 diamond, 49.3 main, 52.8 extended at $0.054 avg.
results.table: Table 7, row OpenHands + CodeActAgent v1.5 + GPT4o, column Diamond Set

results.claim: Project traction: 32K GitHub stars, 2.1K contributions, 188 contributors.
results.quote: OpenHands has gained significant traction, with 32K GitHub stars and more than 2.1K contributions from over 188 contributors.

limits: No ablation ties any score to the event stream, runtime or AgentSkills.
No sandbox security evaluation; isolation is asserted only.
No variance, CIs or repeat runs; baselines mix models and were not stated to be re-run.
Subsets used throughout (SWE Lite, ML-Bench quarter, ToolQA easy, GAIA L1, BIRD 300).
Mixed agent versions v1.5 and v1.8.
Authors concede: agents struggle on complex tasks, suffer when editing long files, workflow needs hand-crafted effort (App A, B).
Models, star counts, versions (runtime v0.9.3, skills v0.6) have dated.
